close_reason: README gotchas at lines 199-200 corrected. The 'sortAsTree/filterAsTree rejected' claim was doubly wrong (these are RFC 8621-specific Email args; the generic handler silently ignores unknown args per RFC 8620 §3.6). The 'in-process filtering only' claim was the opposite of the actual behavior — filter/sort are delegated to JmapBackend::query_objects per handlers.rs:251-268 and per the trait doc that mandates push-down. Commit 3cffaaa.
description:
crate-jmap-server/README.md:200:

  - **In-process filtering only.** `handle_query` fetches all objects and filters them in-process. For large accounts this is O(N) in the number of objects. Backends that can push filtering to storage should implement `query_objects` with real filter logic rather than relying on the generic handler.

This contradicts the actual code:

1. crate-jmap-server/src/handlers.rs:251-268 — handle_query passes filter, sort, limit, position directly to backend.query_objects(). No in-process filtering happens in the handler.

2. crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:1032-1044 — the JmapBackend::query_objects trait doc explicitly says:

   > Implementations MUST honour the supplied `filter` and `sort` arguments
   > efficiently — typically by pushing both into the indexed storage layer
   > (database WHERE / ORDER BY, search index, etc.). Returning every
   > matching id and relying on the caller to paginate after the fact
   > degenerates to O(n) per page for IMAP-migration accounts.
   >
   > Handler implementations in `jmap-*-server` crates SHOULD NOT
   > post-filter or post-sort the backend's result; doing so re-introduces
   > the O(n) cost this method exists to avoid.

The gotcha is a contract claim the kit doesn't actually make. A consumer reading the README learns that handle_query is O(N) and decides not to use it, missing that the actual contract is the opposite — the backend trait MANDATES push-down filtering.

Worse: the gotcha actively misleads about the kit's posture. A consumer who reads this gotcha and decides to write a custom handler 'because handle_query is O(N)' is duplicating work the foundation already does correctly.

This is a docs-as-contract failure: the published documentation is wrong, the documented behaviour is the opposite of the actual behaviour, and the api-contract risk is that consumers will write defensive code around a non-existent limitation.

Fix:

Replace the gotcha with the actual behaviour:

  - **Filter / sort are delegated to the backend.** `handle_query` parses
    `filter` and `sort` from method args into the trait's `O::Filter` and
    `O::Comparator` types, then passes them through `JmapBackend::query_objects`.
    The backend MUST push filter and sort into indexed storage; the handler
    does no in-process re-filtering. Backends that cannot push filter logic
    into storage will hit the contract documented on `JmapBackend::query_objects`.

The other gotcha on line 199 also overpromises: `sortAsTree` and `filterAsTree` are rejected by the generic handler — but looking at handlers.rs:217-285 I do not see explicit rejection of those fields. They appear to be silently passed through to the backend trait (which has no Filter/Comparator variant for them). The 'rejects with unsupportedSort/unsupportedFilter' claim is also potentially stale; cross-check before fixing.

Priority P2 under api-contract,docs because the documented contract directly contradicts the implementation and consumers WILL write defensive code around the wrong contract.
title: README gotcha 'handle_query fetches all objects and filters them in-process' contradicts current code
